## Variance Analysis

### 1. Launch-readiness variance

**Finding:** The project has not demonstrated the minimum conditions to authorize staging or participant use. The Gate 1 pack explicitly marks target environment, staging, deployment, rollback, storage, HTTPS, backup, monitoring, email, and ownership as blocked or open. [Type: Fact] [Source: `application/environment/gate-1-environment-and-ownership.md`, lines 5-26 and 46-92]

**Consequence:** Local implementation can continue to improve the product, but it cannot by itself support a safe launch commitment. [Type: AI-generated assessment] [Sources: `application/environment/local-development.md`, lines 41-58; `workspace/references/deployment-rules.md`, lines 8-19]

**Recommended response:** Make completion and validation of the existing Gate 1 evidence the first control priority. Keep SharePoint available until the custom application passes the approved gates. [Type: AI-generated recommendation] [Sources: `pm-control/registers/action-log.md`, lines 64-72; `artifacts/lead-lab-web-app-delivery-plan.md`, lines 202-214]

### 2. Schedule variance

**Finding:** The project has conditional dates but no approved schedule baseline. The previous schedule review states that Gate 1 remains blocked, the 2026-09-07 launch target conflicts with the 2026-09-07 through 2026-09-09 production-preparation window, and the conditional dates are not credible from current evidence. [Type: Fact] [Source: `pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, lines 24-32]

**Conflict:** The external delivery plan uses a different proposed sequence, including a 2026-09-06 go/no-go and 2026-09-10 launch, while current PM Control records use 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-07 as conditional targets. [Type: Conflict] [Sources: `artifacts/lead-lab-web-app-delivery-plan.md`, lines 84-97 and 139-151; `pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 19-21 and 66]

**Consequence:** A new committed date or baseline would overstate confidence. [Type: AI-generated assessment] [Source: `pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, lines 26-32]

**Recommended response:** Resolve Gate 1 and the schedule-date conflict, then refresh the conditional forecast before the 2026-09-04 go/no-go. Do not establish a baseline in this run. [Type: AI-generated recommendation] [Sources: `pm-control/project-control.md`, line 21; `pm-control/process-register.md`, lines 23-25]

### 3. Technical and operational variance

**Finding:** Deployment research recommends a stack, but it is candidate research and contains unresolved alternatives. The queue guidance conflicts on database queue with one worker versus Redis with two workers; TLS, email provider, alert routing, monitoring, and backup destination also require decisions. [Type: Conflict] [Sources: `artifacts/deployment-research/SYNTHESIS.md`, lines 7-22 and 146-156; `pm-control/registers/issues-log.md`, line 10]

**Consequence:** Implementing the research without Gate 1 validation could create queue locking, duplicate delivery, mail, backup, monitoring, or supply-chain problems. [Type: AI-generated assessment] [Sources: `artifacts/deployment-research/SYNTHESIS.md`, lines 73-111 and 158-166; `pm-control/registers/risk-register.md`, lines 42-48]

**Recommended response:** Treat the research as input only. Validate each choice against the actual Laravel application, target environment, participant-data rules, and authorized decisions before implementation. [Type: AI-generated recommendation] [Sources: `pm-control/registers/action-log.md`, lines 104-115; `pm-control/registers/dependencies-log.md`, lines 30-34]

3. Decide at the go/no-go whether the custom application can proceed or SharePoint remains the delivery path if the required gates are not met.
4. Confirm whether current-facing documentation should be aligned to Season and whether the risk-summary count should be corrected before it is used as a measure.
